--- title: "Strings & Regex" subtitle: "≈ stringr · R4DS strings & regular expressions" jupyter: python3 --- Every Polars string function lives in one namespace, `.str`, on an expression. The [cheatsheet](../overview/polars-cheatsheet.qmd#sec-cs-strings) maps stringr to it function by function; this chapter covers what a one-to-one table hides. The regex engine is a different one (Rust `regex`, not ICU), a pattern can differ per row, offsets come in two units, and Thai text shows that a "character" is not what you see. Splitting a string into columns is in [Reshaping](../transform/reshape.qmd#sec-rs-strings). ## In tidyverse {#sec-str-tidyverse} ```r library(tidyverse) x <- c("CT chest: 5 mm nodule", "MRI brain 3 T", "CT ช่องท้อง 2.5 ซม.") str_detect(x, "CT") # pattern = ICU regex by default str_detect(x, fixed(".")) # fixed() / coll() / regex() modify it str_extract(x, "\\d+(?= mm)") # look-ahead: ICU supports it str_extract(x, "(\\d+) mm", group = 1) # or capture a group (stringr ≥ 1.5) str_replace(x, "(\\w+) (\\w+)", "\\2 \\1") # back-references as \\1 str_replace_all(x, c("CT" = "computed tomography", "MRI" = "magnetic resonance")) str_length("ท้อง") # 4: code points, not what you see str_sub(x, 1, 2) # 1-based, end inclusive ``` stringr vectorises over string *and* pattern, and the pattern is ICU regex unless wrapped. Polars keeps the vectorisation and swaps the engine: two ICU features are gone, `\\1` becomes `$1`, and lengths and offsets need a unit. ## Mental model {#sec-str-model} ```text pl.col("report").str.contains( pattern , literal=False ) └──── Expr ────┘ └ns┘└ method ┘ └──┬──┘ ├── "CT|MRI" one pattern, compiled once, used on every row └── pl.col("pat") one pattern per row (stringr's vectorised pattern) a regex pattern ──► Rust `regex` crate: linear time, Unicode-aware by default, no look-around, no back-references ``` The same `pattern` argument means different things to different methods: | The pattern is… | Methods | stringr analogue | |---|---|---| | a regex; `literal=True` opts out | `contains`, `find`, `count_matches`, `replace`, `replace_all` | default; `fixed()` | | always a regex | `extract`, `extract_all`, `extract_groups` | default | | literal; `literal=False` opts in | `split` | — | | always literal | `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `strip_prefix`, `strip_suffix` | `fixed()` | | a set of characters | `strip_chars`, `strip_chars_start`, `strip_chars_end` | — | | many literals at once (Aho-Corasick) | `contains_any`, `extract_many`, `find_many`, `replace_many` | `fixed()` + `|` | : How `.str` methods read their pattern {.striped} | | stringr (ICU) | Polars (Rust `regex`) | |---|---|---| | Look-ahead/behind `(?=…)`, `(?<=…)` | yes | parse error (@sec-str-engine) | | Back-reference `\1` inside a pattern | yes | parse error | | Group reference in a replacement | `\\1` | `$1`, `${name}`, `$0` (@sec-str-replace) | | Options | `regex(ignore_case =, multiline =, dotall =, comments =)` | inline flags `(?i)`, `(?m)`, `(?s)`, `(?x)` | | `\d`, `\w`, `\b` | Unicode | Unicode: `๑๒` is `\d` | | `[[:alpha:]]` | Unicode | **ASCII only** | | Positions | 1-based, end inclusive | 0-based `(offset, length)` | | Length unit | code points | code points (`len_chars`); `find` returns **bytes** | | Matching | backtracking | linear time in the input, no catastrophic patterns | : The engines side by side {.striped} ## Mechanics {#sec-str-mechanics} ::: {#8ed8ab29 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import re import polars as pl from pl_notes import datasets pl.Config.set_fmt_str_lengths(60) # show long strings in full pl.Config.set_fmt_table_cell_list_len(6) planes_df = datasets.planes() airports_df = datasets.airports() flights_df = datasets.flights() reports_df = pl.DataFrame({"report": [ # invented, report-like snippets "CT chest: 5 mm nodule in RUL. No pneumothorax.", "CXR: small left pleural effusion.", "CXR: no effusion or pneumothorax.", "MRI brain 3 T: no no acute infarct.", "CT: Pneumothorax, large. Nodules 3 mm and 4.5 mm.", "CT ช่องท้อง: ก้อนที่ตับ 2.5 ซม.", ]}) ``` ::: ### Patterns per row {#sec-str-per-row} Pass an expression as the pattern and each row gets its own. Which aircraft tail numbers end in their carrier's code? ::: {#696bedde .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} tails_df = flights_df.select("carrier", "tailnum").unique().drop_nulls() tails_df.group_by("carrier").agg( n_planes=pl.len(), ends_in_code=pl.col("tailnum").str.ends_with(pl.col("carrier")).mean().round(2), ).sort("ends_in_code", "carrier", descending=[True, False]).head(6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
shape: (6, 3)
carriern_planesends_in_code

"AA"6001.0
"AS"841.0
"HA"141.0
"MQ"2371.0
"WN"5820.48
"UA"6200.45
``` ::: ::: American (`N619AA`) always does; Southwest about half the time. Not every method takes a per-row pattern: | Per-row expression accepted | Not accepted (Polars 2.0) | |---|---| | `contains`, `find`, `count_matches`, `extract`, `extract_all`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `split`, `strip_prefix`, `strip_suffix`, `strip_chars` | `replace` / `replace_all` **pattern**: "dynamic pattern length … not supported yet" (the replacement *value* may vary) | | `extract_many`: a List column of keywords per row | `contains_any`: one list for all rows only ("not yet implemented") | | numbers: `head(n)`, `slice(offset, length)`, `pad_start(length)`, `to_integer(base=)` | `extract_groups`: a `str` only (`TypeError`) | : Verified on Polars 2.0.0 {.striped} To drop the code from `tailnum`, `replace(pl.col("carrier"), "")` fails, but `strip_suffix(pl.col("carrier"))` works. The string side must be a full column too: `pl.lit("text").str.extract_all(pl.col("pattern"))` fails with a length mismatch instead of broadcasting. ### The regex engine {#sec-str-engine} The Rust `regex` crate guarantees matching in linear time. The price is two features it can't offer within that guarantee: ::: {#fc013ec4 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} reports_df.select(pl.col("report").str.extract(r"\d+(?= mm)", 0)) # look-ahead ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
ComputeError: regex error: regex parse error:
    \d+(?= mm)
       ^^^
error: look-around, including look-ahead and look-behind, is not supported

This error occurred in the following expression:
	col("report").str.extract(["\d+(?= mm)"])
``` ::: ::: ::: A back-reference such as `\b(\w+) \1\b` fails the same way, with "error: backreferences are not supported". Both errors come from the regex parser, not from the data. The workaround: match the context instead of looking at it, and capture the part you want. | ICU pattern | Without look-around or back-references | |---|---| | `\d+(?= mm)` | `extract(r"(\d+) mm", 1)` | | `pneumothorax` not preceded by `no` | `contains("pneumothorax") & ~contains(r"\bno\b[^.]*pneumothorax")` (recipe in @sec-str-recipes) | | `\b(\w+) \1\b` (doubled word) | split into words, compare each with the previous one | : Workarounds {.striped} ::: {#b1d8948c .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} reports_df.select( "report", size_mm=pl.col("report").str.extract(r"(\d+(?:\.\d+)?) mm", 1), doubled_word=pl.col("report").str.to_lowercase().str.extract_all(r"\w+") .list.eval(pl.element() == pl.element().shift(1)).list.any(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: **Unicode classes.** Character classes are Unicode-aware by default. One mixed string against several classes (a per-row pattern again): ::: {#bc81e147 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} classes_df = pl.DataFrame({ "pattern": [r"\d+", r"[0-9]+", r"\w+", r"\p{L}+", r"[[:alpha:]]+", r"\p{Thai}+", r"\p{Latin}+"] }) classes_df.with_columns(text=pl.lit("CT ช่องท้อง ๑๒ mm, Ünal 7")).select( "pattern", matches=pl.col("text").str.extract_all(pl.col("pattern")) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
shape: (7, 2)
patternmatches
strlist[str]
"\d+"["๑๒", "7"]
"[0-9]+"["7"]
"\w+"["CT", "ช่องท้อง", "๑๒", "mm", "Ünal", "7"]
"\p{L}+"["CT", "ช", "องท", "อง", "mm", "Ünal"]
"[[:alpha:]]+"["CT", "mm", "nal"]
"\p{Thai}+"["ช่องท้อง", "๑๒"]
"\p{Latin}+"["CT", "mm", "Ünal"]
``` ::: ::: - `\d` matches Thai digits (`๑๒`); `[0-9]` or `(?-u:\d)` is ASCII only. - `\p{L}` breaks Thai words apart: tone marks and above/below vowels are marks (`\p{M}`), not letters. `\w` and `\p{Thai}` keep them. - `[[:alpha:]]` is ASCII only, so `Ünal` loses its `Ü` (ICU's is Unicode). - `\p{Thai}` is a script, so it includes Thai digits; `\X` (grapheme) is a parse error. **Flags.** stringr's `regex()` options become inline flags at the start of the pattern, or scoped to a group with `(?i:…)`: | stringr | Polars | Effect | |---|---|---| | `regex(p, ignore_case = TRUE)` | `(?i)p` | Unicode case folding: `(?i)ünal` matches `ÜNAL` | | `regex(p, multiline = TRUE)` | `(?m)p` | `^` and `$` match at each line | | `regex(p, dotall = TRUE)` | `(?s)p` | `.` also matches `\n` | | `regex(p, comments = TRUE)` | `(?x)p` | whitespace and `# …` ignored; escape a space as `\ ` | : Options become flags {.striped} ::: {#2b1c5144 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} note_s = pl.Series(["FINDINGS:\nSmall nodule.\nIMPRESSION:\nNo acute finding."]) { "no flag": note_s.str.extract(r"FINDINGS:(.*)IMPRESSION", 1).item(), "(?s)": note_s.str.extract(r"(?s)FINDINGS:\s*(.*?)\s*IMPRESSION", 1).item(), "(?m)": note_s.str.extract_all(r"(?m)^[A-Z]+:").item().to_list(), "(?xs)": note_s.str.extract(r"""(?xs) IMPRESSION: \s* # the heading (.+) # everything after it """, 1).item(), } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` {'no flag': None, '(?s)': 'Small nodule.', '(?m)': ['FINDINGS:', 'IMPRESSION:'], '(?xs)': 'No acute finding.'} ``` ::: ::: Without `(?s)`, `.` stops at the newline and the match fails. ### Detect {#sec-str-detect} Many keywords: `contains_any()` (Aho-Corasick, literal) or one regex alternation. ::: {#5a9ebe9c .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} findings = ["nodule", "effusion", "pneumothorax"] findings_re = r"(?i)\b(?:" + "|".join(map(re.escape, findings)) + ")" reports_df.select( "report", aho=pl.col("report").str.contains_any(findings, ascii_case_insensitive=True), regex=pl.col("report").str.contains(findings_re), which=pl.col("report").str.extract_many(findings, ascii_case_insensitive=True), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: | | `contains_any` / `extract_many` | `contains` with `a|b|c` | |---|---|---| | Patterns | literal strings | regex (escape with `re.escape()`, or `.str.escape_regex()` on a column) | | Case-insensitive | `ascii_case_insensitive=True`: **ASCII only** | `(?i)`: Unicode | | Word boundaries | none: `"CT"` matches inside `"CTA"` | `\b` | | Reports which keyword | `extract_many` | `extract_all` | : Many keywords {.striped} Overlapping keywords: by default the match that *ends* first wins, not the longest; `leftmost=True` takes the leftmost start, then the first-listed keyword: ::: {#699aef86 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} cta_s = pl.Series(["CTA chest"]) { "default": cta_s.str.extract_many(["CTA", "CT", "C"]).item().to_list(), "leftmost=True": cta_s.str.extract_many(["CTA", "CT", "C"], leftmost=True).item().to_list(), } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ``` {'default': ['C'], 'leftmost=True': ['CTA']} ``` ::: ::: Rule: list longer keywords first and pass `leftmost=True`. The same applies to `replace_many()`. For patterns typed by users, `contains(pattern, strict=False)` turns an invalid regex into null instead of an error. ### Extract {#sec-str-extract} | stringr | Polars | Returns | |---|---|---| | `str_extract(x, p)` | `extract(p, 0)` | String, the whole match | | `str_extract(x, p, group = 1)` | `extract(p)`: group 1 is the **default** | String | | `str_extract_all(x, p)` | `extract_all(p)` | List(String), always whole matches | | `str_match(x, p)` | `extract_groups(p)` | Struct, one field per group, first match only | : Extracting {.striped} ::: {#c87dedbc .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} size_re = r"(\d+(?:\.\d+)?) ?(mm|cm|ซม)" reports_df.select( "report", group1=pl.col("report").str.extract(size_re), whole=pl.col("report").str.extract(size_re, 0), every=pl.col("report").str.extract_all(size_re), no_group=pl.col("report").str.extract(r"\d+ mm"), # group 1 doesn't exist → null ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}

"CXR: small left pleural effusion."nullnull[]null
"CXR: no effusion or pneumothorax."nullnull[]null
"MRI brain 3 T: no no acute infarct."nullnull[]null
"CT: Pneumothorax, large. Nodules 3 mm and 4.5 mm.""3""3 mm"["3 mm", "4.5 mm"]null

``` ::: ::: `no_group` is all null and nothing warns: with the default `group_index=1`, a pattern without a group extracts nothing. A group number that doesn't exist does the same. `extract_groups()` names fields after named groups, `(?…)` or `(?P…)`; unnamed groups become `"1"`, `"2"`, …; `unnest()` makes them columns (recipe in @sec-str-recipes; more in [Reshaping](../transform/reshape.qmd#sec-rs-names)). Every match of a group (≈ `str_match_all()`): extract all whole matches, then run an expression on each list element with `list.eval()` (see [Nested Data](nested.qmd)): ::: {#366bdbdc .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} reports_df.select( "report", sizes_mm=pl.col("report").str.extract_all(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)? mm") .list.eval(pl.element().str.extract(r"([\d.]+)").cast(pl.Float64)), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ```{=html}

"CT ช่องท้อง: ก้อนที่ตับ 2.5 ซม."[]
``` ::: ::: ### Replace {#sec-str-replace} The replacement string uses `$`, not `\`: ::: {#df7b5f8d .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} dates_s = pl.Series(["2025-03-14"]) iso_re = r"(?\d{4})-(?\d{2})-(?\d{2})" { "$3/$2/$1": dates_s.str.replace(iso_re, "$3/$2/$1").item(), "${d}.${m}.${y}": dates_s.str.replace(iso_re, "${d}.${m}.${y}").item(), "<$0>": dates_s.str.replace(r"\d+", "<$0>").item(), r"\3/\2/\1": dates_s.str.replace(iso_re, r"\3/\2/\1").item(), "$1x": dates_s.str.replace(iso_re, "$1x").item(), "${1}x": dates_s.str.replace(iso_re, "${1}x").item(), "US$$": dates_s.str.replace(iso_re, "US$$").item(), } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ``` {'$3/$2/$1': '14/03/2025', '${d}.${m}.${y}': '14.03.2025', '<$0>': '<2025>-03-14', '\\3/\\2/\\1': '\\3/\\2/\\1', '$1x': '', '${1}x': '2025x', 'US$$': 'US$'} ``` ::: ::: - `\3` is not a reference: it is inserted literally. - `$1x` refers to a group named `1x`, which doesn't exist, so it inserts nothing. Use braces: `${1}x`. - A literal `$` is `$$`, or pass `literal=True`, which turns off `$` expansion as well as the regex. A replacement taken from a column (`pl.col("value")`) is expanded too. `replace()` replaces the first match and `replace_all()` every match, as in stringr. `n=` replaces the first *n*, but only for a literal pattern (`replace(".", "-", literal=True, n=2)` turns `1.2.3.4` into `1-2-3.4`): ::: {#b3859c72 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.Series(["1 2 3 4"]).str.replace(r"\d", "#", n=2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
ComputeError: regex replacement with 'n > 1' not yet supported

This error occurred in the following expression:
	col("").str.replace(["\d", "#"])
``` ::: ::: ::: **`replace_many()`** ≈ `str_replace_all()` with a named vector, with three differences: patterns are literal, all of them are applied in **one pass**, and a single replacement must still be a list: ::: {#7eb1c765 .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} exam_s = pl.Series(["CT and MRI"]) { "mapping (swap)": exam_s.str.replace_many({"CT": "MRI", "MRI": "CT"}).item(), "many → one": exam_s.str.replace_many(["CT", "MRI"], [""]).item(), } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=14} ``` {'mapping (swap)': 'MRI and CT', 'many → one': ' and '} ``` ::: ::: stringr applies a named vector in turn, so `str_replace_all("CT and MRI", c(CT = "MRI", MRI = "CT"))` gives `"CT and CT"`. One pass makes the swap work. A bare string as the replacement (`replace_many(["CT", "MRI"], "")`) raises "Use `implode` to wrap the string value into a list"; and a bare string as the *patterns* argument is read as a column name (@sec-str-gotchas). ### Length and Unicode {#sec-str-unicode} ::: {#b8f48356 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} organs_df = pl.DataFrame({"word": ["ปอด", "ท้อง", "น้ำ", "กระดูกสันหลัง", "lung", "café"]}) organs_df.with_columns( chars=pl.col("word").str.len_chars(), bytes=pl.col("word").str.len_bytes(), head2=pl.col("word").str.head(2), slice_1_1=pl.col("word").str.slice(1, 1), reversed=pl.col("word").str.reverse(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ```text ท้อง = ท ◌้ อ ง len_chars() = 4 (code points; = str_length()) U+0E17 U+0E49 U+0E2D U+0E07 len_bytes() = 12 (3 bytes each in UTF-8) letter mark (Mn) letter letter what you see = 3 cells ``` - `len_chars()` counts code points, like `str_length()`, so a tone mark or above/below vowel counts as a character. - `head()`, `tail()` and `slice()` cut between code points: `slice(1, 1)` of `ท้อง` is a lone tone mark; `head(2)` of `น้ำ` drops the final vowel. - `reverse()` is the exception: it keeps a base character and its marks together (`งอท้`, where a code-point reversal gives `งอ้ท`). - Polars has no grapheme-cluster length (`\X` is not supported). The number of visible cells is close to `len_chars() - count_matches(r"\p{Mn}")`. **`find()` returns a byte offset**, while `slice()` takes characters. On ASCII the two agree; on Thai they don't: ::: {#19ff82fe .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.DataFrame({"s": ["CT chest 5 mm", "CT ช่องท้อง 5 mm"]}).with_columns( at=pl.col("s").str.find(r"\d"), sliced=pl.col("s").str.slice(pl.col("s").str.find(r"\d")), # wrong on Thai extracted=pl.col("s").str.extract(r"(\d.*)", 1), # right ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=16} ```{=html}

To cut at a pattern, extract or split with a regex instead of computing an offset. **Normalization.** One visible string can have several encodings, and they compare unequal. Two spellings each of `café` and Thai `คำ`: ::: {#1501ee79 .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} variants_df = pl.DataFrame({"term": ["caf\u00e9", "cafe\u0301", "ค\u0e33", "ค\u0e4d\u0e32"]}) variants_df.select( distinct_raw=pl.col("term").n_unique(), distinct_nfc=pl.col("term").str.normalize("NFC").n_unique(), distinct_nfkc=pl.col("term").str.normalize("NFKC").n_unique(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=17} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: `é` precomposed (U+00E9) and `e` + combining acute (U+0301) become one under NFC. Thai SARA AM (`ำ`, U+0E33) and NIKHAHIT + SARA AA (`ํ` + `า`), a common typing variant of the same vowel, become one only under NFKC, because SARA AM's decomposition is a compatibility one. Normalize the patterns as well: after NFKC, a literal `"คำ"` typed in Python no longer matches the column (`unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", "คำ")` does). **Case.** ::: {#ce3bf7aa .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.DataFrame({"s": ["straße", "mri ของ สมอง", "x-ray of l1", "ct3d DICOM-RT", "o'neil mcdonald"]}).with_columns( upper=pl.col("s").str.to_uppercase(), title=pl.col("s").str.to_titlecase(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=18} ```{=html}

NBSP zeros=pl.col("s").str.strip_chars_start("0"), # "000" → "" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=19} ```{=html}

An offset past the end gives `""`; a negative `length` in `slice()` is an error. **Interpolate.** `pl.format()` accepts glue-style named placeholders, which refer to columns directly, as well as `{}` (next argument) and `{0}` (by position): ::: {#0c381634 .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} exams_df = pl.DataFrame({"modality": ["CT", "MRI", None], "region": ["chest", "brain", "knee"], "slice_mm": [5.0, 1.25, 3.0]}) exams_df.select( named=pl.format("{modality} {region}, {slice_mm} mm"), positional=pl.format("{} ({})", "region", "modality"), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=21} ```{=html}

str_length(b)` can be negative | `UInt32` wraps: `ปอด` − `ท้อง` = 4294967295 ([Data Model](../core/data-model.qmd#sec-dm-unsigned)) | cast to `Int64` first | | a string argument is a value | `contains_any("x")` reads `"x"` as a column | pass a list | | stringr works on factors | `.str` on a `Categorical` raises "expected String type, got: cat" ([Categorical & Enum](categorical.qmd)) | `cast(pl.String)` | : The differences at a glance {.striped} ### `"."` matches everything {#sec-str-dot} ::: {#b46c2260 .cell execution_count=24} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.Series(["v1.2", "v102", "v1-2"]).str.contains("1.2").to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=24} ``` [True, True, True] ``` ::: ::: ### `replace_many()` has no word boundaries {#sec-str-substrings} Expanding the abbreviations in `airports.name` (`Intl`, `Rgnl`, `Muni`, …) with `replace_many()` also rewrites every word that *contains* one: ::: {#30c195c1 .cell execution_count=25} ``` {.python .cell-code} abbreviations = {"Intl": "International", "Rgnl": "Regional", "Muni": "Municipal", "Fld": "Field", "Co": "County"} name_expanded = pl.col("name") for short, full in abbreviations.items(): name_expanded = name_expanded.str.replace_all(rf"\b{short}\b", full) airports_df_damaged = airports_df.select( "faa", "name", aho=pl.col("name").str.replace_many(abbreviations), regex=name_expanded, ).filter(pl.col("aho") != pl.col("regex")) print(airports_df_damaged.height, "names damaged") airports_df_damaged.sort("faa").select("faa", "aho", "regex").head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 271 names damaged ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=25} ```{=html}

Precise Thai matching needs word segmentation, which Polars doesn't do. ### Strings that are column names {#sec-str-colname} ::: {#cde2b6f1 .cell execution_count=27} ``` {.python .cell-code} reports_df.select(pl.col("report").str.contains_any("effusion")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
ColumnNotFoundError: unable to find column "effusion"; valid columns: ["report"]
``` ::: ::: ::: `contains_any()`, `extract_many()` and `replace_many()` take their patterns as expression input, so a bare string is a column (the rule in [Expressions](../core/expressions.qmd#sec-expr-literals)). A list is a value. ## Recipes {#sec-str-recipes} **Collapse manufacturer variants** in `planes` (`AIRBUS` vs `AIRBUS INDUSTRIE`). One anchored regex removes any run of company suffixes; list longer alternatives before their prefixes: ::: {#15d8651e .cell execution_count=28} ``` {.python .cell-code} suffix_re = r"(?: (?:INDUSTRIE|AIRCRAFT CO|CORPORATION|CORP|INC|LTD|CO))+$" planes_df_clean = planes_df.with_columns(maker=pl.col("manufacturer").str.replace(suffix_re, "")) print(planes_df["manufacturer"].n_unique(), "→", planes_df_clean["maker"].n_unique()) with pl.Config(fmt_str_lengths=90, tbl_width_chars=120): print( planes_df_clean.group_by("maker").agg( n=pl.len(), variants=pl.col("manufacturer").unique().sort().str.join(" | "), ).filter(pl.col("variants").str.contains("|", literal=True)).sort("maker") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 35 → 31 shape: (3, 3) ┌───────────────────┬─────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ maker ┆ n ┆ variants │ │ --- ┆ --- ┆ --- │ │ str ┆ u32 ┆ str │ ╞═══════════════════╪═════╪═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╡ │ AIRBUS ┆ 736 ┆ AIRBUS | AIRBUS INDUSTRIE │ │ CANADAIR ┆ 10 ┆ CANADAIR | CANADAIR LTD │ │ MCDONNELL DOUGLAS ┆ 237 ┆ MCDONNELL DOUGLAS | MCDONNELL DOUGLAS AIRCRAFT CO | MCDONNELL DOUGLAS CORPORATION │ └───────────────────┴─────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ::: ::: Three makers absorb seven spellings. The `$` anchor is not decorative: without it, `" CO"` cuts into any word that starts with `CO` (`"ACME COMPANY CO"` → `"ACMEMPANY CO"`). **A number with its unit, from free text in two languages.** Translate Thai digits first, then capture value and unit, then convert: ::: {#13519182 .cell execution_count=29} ``` {.python .cell-code} findings_df = pl.DataFrame({"finding": [ "CT chest: 5 mm slices", "Nodule 0.6cm in RUL", "Thyroid nodule 12.5 mm, TI-RADS 3", "ก้อนที่ตับ ขนาด ๑.๕ ซม.", "No measurable lesion", ]}) mm_per_unit = {"mm": 1, "มม": 1, "cm": 10, "ซม": 10} findings_df.with_columns( size=pl.col("finding").str.replace_many(thai_digits) .str.extract_groups(r"(?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?mm|cm|มม|ซม)") ).unnest("size").with_columns( size_mm=pl.col("value").cast(pl.Float64) * pl.col("unit").replace_strict(mm_per_unit), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=29} ```{=html}
